newsitem.title: USA: Mitchell to buy back shrs/retire debt.
newsitem.headline: Mitchell to buy back shrs/retire debt.

text.p: Mitchell Energy & Development Corp said Monday that it will use the $460 million of net after-tax proceeds realized from the just-completed sale of its real estate subsidiary to repurchase common stock, retire public debt, make asset acquisitions and increase capital spending.
Mitchell said it has allocated $100 million to buy back its common stock.

The company already has repurchased 700,000 A shares and 1,400,000 B shares from a financial intermediary through an accelerated stock purchase transaction, leaving about 22.4 million A shares and 27.4 million B shares outstanding.
Total consideration was $50 million, subject to a market price adjustment provision, Mitchell said.
In addition to the accelerated stock purchase, Mitchell said it also will spend as much as $50 million to directly buy back shares of both A and B stock from time to time in open market purchases.

The company said it also plans to spend about $200 million, including a premium, to retire outstanding public debt through a tender offer announced today for a portion of its 9-1/4 percent senior notes.
Mitchell said it is tendering for up to $180 million principal amount of its outstanding 9-1/4 percent Senior Notes due January 15, 2002.
The offer commenced today and will expire Sept. 16, unless extended.

The purchase price to be paid for the 9-1/4 percent senior notes tendered will be based equal to a fixed spread of 30 basis points over the yield to maturity on the 6-1/8 percent U.S. Treasury Note due December 31, 2001, as of 1400 EDT/1800 GMT on September 11, 1997.
In addition, the company said it will pay accrued and unpaid interest.

The remaining proceeds will be used to make acquisitions of producing energy properties as well as gas gathering and processing facilities that complement existing operations and to increase the pace of exploration and development under the company's capital spending program, Mitchell said.
Separately, the company said it expects to realize an additional $30 million from the sale of its remaining non-Woodlands real estate assets during the next six to 12 months.
